title: Flat limits and finite tensors of sectionwise adic algebra towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $R=\underline A$ the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $(S_m)_{m\geq1}$ be a strict inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative $A$-algebras, with $I^mS_m=0$. Assume, for every object $U$, that $S_m(U)$ is flat over $A/I^m$, every transition $S_{m+1}(U)\to S_m(U)$ is surjective, and for all $m,n\geq1$ the transition to $S_{\min(m,n)}(U)$ induces an isomorphism $S_m(U)\otimes_A A/I^n\cong S_{\min(m,n)}(U)$. Put $B=\lim_m S_m$ as a ring sheaf [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Then $B$ is flat over $R$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every finitely generated $A$-module $F$, the canonical sectionwise maps give isomorphisms
$$B(U)\otimes_A F\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim_m(S_m(U)\otimes_A F),$$
natural in $U$ and $F$. For every $n\geq1$, the original projection $B\to S_n$ induces an isomorphism $B/I^nB\xrightarrow{\sim}S_n$. These quotient isomorphisms commute with all transitions. The quotient is the cokernel of the action of the ideal generated by the constant sections of $I^n$; tensor products of modules of sections are ordinary module tensor products, while tensor products of sheaves mean sheafified module tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and flatness means exactness of tensoring in the category of sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Evaluate the ring-sheaf limit using preservation of limits by Under.forget, sheafToPresheaf, evaluation, and the forgetful functor to types. Reflect this limit in ModuleCat A and identify it with the module limit by its unique projection-preserving linear equivalence. Apply ModuleCat.limit_flat_of_flat_quotients objectwise and swap tensor factors. Transport injectivity and surjectivity onto compatible families through these equivalences. Compatibility of comparison images follows from limit.w; naturality in F and U is checked on pure tensors. A recursive lift of each section through the surjective tower gives surjectivity of every original projection.

source.place: Tag 0912 (lemma-limit-flat); sectionwise evaluation as in Tag 093M (sites-modules-lemma-completion-flat)

proof.text: Use the local finite relation criterion for sheaf flatness. The constant-presheaf sheafification unit is locally surjective. Intersect the finitely many covering image sieves of the coefficients of a relation in B. On every arrow of this cover lift those coefficients to A; the relation becomes an A-module relation in B(V). Sectionwise flatness from Step 1 and the ordinary flat-module equational criterion factor it through finitely many elements with zero coefficient relations. Map the factorization coefficients through the constant-section ring map. This satisfies the local relation criterion, hence proves IsFlatOnSite. Empty finite relations and empty covering sieves are included.

source.place: Tags 093M and 08FC (lemma-flat-eq); local lifting along constant-presheaf sheafification

proof.text: Fix n. The n-th projection is surjective by the recursive lifting argument of Step 1. Identify its kernel with I^(n+1)B(U). One inclusion follows from the quotient scalar tower, which annihilates I^(n+1). Conversely, suppose pi_n(b)=0. Every earlier projection vanishes. For every m the reduction equivalence in the hypotheses sends pi_m(b) tensor 1 to pi_min(m,n)(b)=0, so that tensor is zero. Injectivity of the finite tensor comparison for A/I^(n+1) gives b tensor 1=0. The canonical quotient-tensor equivalence identifies this with the vanishing of the class of b in B(U)/I^(n+1)B(U). The first isomorphism theorem now gives a ring equivalence normalized by the original projection.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), quotient argument, using Tag 0912 and the additional reduction compatibility assumed here

proof.text: Build the sheaf-module morphism q from the original ring-sheaf projection, with scalar linearity following from Under.w. For any sheaf-module map f annihilating all products a*b for a in I^(n+1), span induction shows f kills the entire extended ideal on every object. Step 3 identifies that ideal with the kernel of q. Factor each f_U through the module quotient by ker(q_U) and the first-isomorphism linear equivalence onto S_n(U). The factors commute with restrictions because q_U is surjective and both composites agree after q_U by naturality of f and q. These sectionwise linear maps define the unique sheaf-module factor. This proves the stated cokernel universal property directly, without a separate sheafification-exactness invocation.

The ring quotient equivalences send the class of b to pi_n(b). Their restriction compatibility is exactly naturality of the original ring-sheaf projection on b. For m >= n, transition compatibility follows from limit.w applied to the arrow m -> n. Thus identity and composite transitions are included with the same normalization.

I read the item in full: 5 steps, base 4ef97b6, and the live node is unsplit with no proof. Statement: only the scope of the tensor convention changed. Tensors of modules of sections such as B(U)⊗F are now ordinary tensors and tensors of sheaves are sheafified, so the base wording no longer fails to type-check. The report names the change and nothing is weakened; the citer constant-completion-equivalence Step 0 uses the ordinary section tensor. Sources: I read Stacks sites-modules 093M (lines 8261-8310), 03ET (lines 4293-4303) and more-algebra 0912 (lines 6475-6484); the item generalizes 093M to a varying tower with the reduction isomorphisms as hypotheses. Step 1: the sectionwise limit (def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit) plus 0912 node, whose hypotheses match exactly; the factor swap and pure-tensor naturality are correct. Step 2: correctly uses the constant presheaf A_p, which is the presheaf O that lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat takes. Presheaf tensor is P(U)⊗_A B(U), and flat-tensor-exact gives preservation of kernels and finite products, including the empty one. Sheafification gives A_p^#=R and B^#=B, so B is flat over R. Step 3: elementary; I checked that the reduction isomorphisms are compatible with transitions (both give a·t(s) at min(m,n)), that the stable tail is S_n, and that the composite is π_n. Step 4: the finitely generated I^n gives the image U↦I^nB(U), equal to the image of the constant ideal action. The presheaf cokernel is isomorphic to the sheaf S_n, and sheafification commutes with cokernels. Step 5: representative check. Edge cases: I=0, I=A, n=1, m<n, objects with empty coverings. Route: sk-thm-p1 is cited by the unit; flat-tensor-exact is a Mathlib leaf. The tool use lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat (picard-semicon), generic flatness under sheafification, is accepted.
